summary: Phanit Jetjiravat is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn (1933–2016) was a sinologist and historian educated at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Professor of History and East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard from 1978.

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester in 1989. Attested in 2010, he served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory at the University of Leeds.

Philip Boas Yampolsky (1920–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya. He served as Adjunct Associate Professor and East Asian Library Librarian at Columbia from 1968 to 1996.

Philip Clart (born 1963) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from ~1991 to 1996. He became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig around 2008.
Philip Deslippe is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He has been a graduate student (attested 2020–2026) and teaching associate (attested 2020) at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Philip Kapleau (1912–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under D.T. Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn (1940–2004) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (~1971–1985) and became John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at Notre Dame in 1985.

Philip Lutgendorf (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who graduated from the University of Chicago. He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Notre Dame and Syracuse University. He taught at Dominican University of California from ~1980 to 2017.

Philip Whalen (1923–2002) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure educated at Reed College who studied under Richard Baker. He served as resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo (~1984–1987) and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn in 2004 under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He has held research positions at Bonn, Vienna, and Leipzig (attested 2022–2025).
Philippe Stern (1895–1979) was an Indologist and art historian. He held posts at the Guimet Museum (1927–1965), the École du Louvre (1929–1965), and the Musée de la parole et du geste.
Philippe Turenne is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University, where he earned his PhD under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of Tibetan at INALCO and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1870–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar of art history, archaeology, and Sinology who completed his PhD at Harvard University under Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018) and became Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat around 1999.

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. Attested in 2012, he served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he was attested as Associate Professor in 2013.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under supervisors Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
